query: Is this trace launch-bound? Would --cuda-graph help?
notes: Kernel-bound: 1% launch cost, 55% busy, 5ms blocked in cudaDeviceSynchronize. Summing the cuda_runtime category instead of matching launch names reports ~101% and inverts the answer. The question is phrased to invite a yes.
expected_behavior: Reports the run as kernel-bound, not launch-bound
Does NOT recommend --cuda-graph
Reads synchronize_ms as the CPU waiting on the GPU rather than as launch cost
Quotes launch_per_device_pct (1.0) rather than describing the result vaguely

query: The GPU looks underused in this profile. What is going on?
notes: Launch-bound: 8% busy, 19 idle gaps, launch cost 400% of device time, synchronize_ms 0. Durations are realistic (12us launches, 3us kernels); the ratio is what matters.
expected_behavior: Runs the device command and reports a low busy_pct with large idle gaps
Follows up with the launch command rather than stopping at 'the GPU is idle'
Concludes the loop is launch-bound and that --cuda-graph is the relevant fix
Does not sum busy_ms across streams into a single utilization figure

query: Which input shapes are the aten::mm calls running on, and how much time does each take?
notes: No fixed command covers this; it needs a join onto args, and the dimensions are int_value. Two shapes share their K and N, so grouping by a single dim key merges them and reports one shape where there are two. Expect 128x512 and 256x512, three calls each.
expected_behavior: Recognizes no fixed command covers this and uses the sql command
Joins args on arg_set_id and reads int_value, not string_value
Assembles the whole shape rather than grouping on one dimension
Reports both shapes with their call counts

query: Where does the time go in this trace?
notes: Real torch output, so the operator nesting is genuine: aten::addmm (692.9us self over 10 calls) sits inside aten::linear, and ranking by inclusive time would put the wrapper on top. CPU-only, so the device commands correctly have nothing to report. Unfiltered, top-ops puts the profiler's own 'PyTorch Profiler (0)' slice first; recognizing that as overhead rather than work is part of the case.
expected_behavior: Runs overview before drawing conclusions
Names aten::addmm as the dominant operator
Ranks by self time, so the wrapper aten::linear does not outrank it
Reports the device commands as having nothing to say on a CPU-only trace, rather than treating zeros as a fault
Does not read or parse the .trace.json.gz file directly

query: Profile Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B for 8 tokens and tell me where the time goes.
notes: End to end, with no trace supplied — the only case that exercises running the profiler and picking up the path it prints. Not deterministic: needs Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (~1.7GB, downloaded if not cached), takes minutes, and the numbers vary by host. Skip when offline.
expected_behavior: Runs `walnut profile` and uses the trace path it printed
Runs overview before drawing conclusions
Ranks operators by self time
Reports where the time actually went with numbers, not just a list of commands
